Unlike traditional transformers that rely heavily on brute-force token prediction, CRT prioritizes contextual coherence, semantic preservation, and sub-symbolic pattern extraction. This neuromorphic philosophy sets CRT apart by emphasizing the importance of understanding context and preserving meaningful information over raw computational power.

Mirus, as a belief-state and evidence packet layer, plays a crucial role in managing the cognitive state within the model. It ensures that the system maintains a coherent and accurate representation of its current knowledge and beliefs. Holden, on the other hand, acts as the speech/rendering layer downstream of Mirus, translating the internal states into understandable outputs.

CRT's reliance on large language models (LLMs) is a limitation that needs to be addressed. To enhance its independence and robustness, we propose focusing more on internal mechanisms such as webhook memory self-training and sub-conscious processing.

The Semantic String Engine (SSE) should indeed be highlighted as a core concept, alongside DNNT (Distributed Neural Network Theory). This mechanism allows CRT to maintain integrity by self-correcting when inconsistencies arise.

By reordering our focus and emphasizing these unique aspects—Mirus for belief-state management, Holden for output rendering, SSE for semantic spine, and DNNT for theoretical underpinning—we can better highlight what makes CRT distinct from other models. The implementation of these concepts involves a layered approach where each component interacts to create a robust and adaptive reasoning system.
